question.text: Which of the following plots is the graph of $y=\tan(x)?$
question.explanation:
Let's recall some of the basic properties of $y=\tan x{:}$

  • The domain of the function is almost $x\in (-\infty ,\infty)$ except for the points where the function is undefined, namely $x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots$

  • The range of the function is $y\in (-\infty, \infty).$

  • The period of the function is $\pi.$

  • There is no minimum or maximum value.

  • The zeros occur at $x=0,\pm\pi,\pm2\pi,\dots$

question.text: Which of the following is a zero of $y=\tan x?$
question.explanation:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\tan x.$

The zeros of the function occur at $x=0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots$

Of the given values, the only one that is a zero of the function is $x=-\pi.$

question.text: Which of the following $x$-values is not in the domain of $y=\tan x?$
question.explanation:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\tan x.$

The domain of the function contains all real numbers except for $x= \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots$

Of the given values, the only one that is not in the domain is $x=-\dfrac{5\pi}{2}.$

question.text: Which of the following plots is the graph of $y=\cot x?$
question.explanation:
Let's recall some of the basic properties of $y=\cot{x}\mathbin{:}$

  • The domain is all real numbers except $x = n\pi$ for any integer $n.$

  • The range is all real numbers, so there is no minimum or maximum.

  • The period of the function is $\pi.$

  • Its zeros occur at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi$ for any integer $n.$

  • $y\to -\infty$ as $x\to\pi^-,$ and $y\to \infty$ as $x\to0^+.$
